key_insight: The paper shows that large language models contain low-overlap functional subnetworks that can be selectively updated to improve continual learning without causing severe forgetting.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a practical way to make continual fine-tuning of LLMs more memory- and compute-efficient by restricting optimization to task-relevant regions.
method: Gradient-attribution profiling identifies cognition-associated subnetworks with minimal mutual overlap.
CiMEO routes each training example to its matching functional subnetwork and updates only those parameters plus their optimizer states.
Subspace-overlap and principal-angle analyses are used to verify representation preservation during sequential training.
evidence_signal: The method is evaluated across 1.4 million sequential instructions and reports the best average performance on five generative benchmarks, including programming, exam-style tasks, and mathematical reasoning.
watch_item: Subnetwork routing depends on reliable functional localization, so performance may be sensitive to attribution quality and how well subnetworks generalize across unseen task mixtures.
paper_title: Functional Subnetwork Localization for Efficient Continual Learning in Large Language Models
